title: Flux Keyboard
intro: Everything Flux Keyboard adds over Pastiera 0.86, Pastiera's final feature release, then what the Pastiera team built between 0.85 and 0.86, which Flux Keyboard includes.

highlights.text: Long-press an app in the quick launcher to add Flux Keyboard's own shortcut for it (call or message a contact from your phone and messages apps, a website from your browser, a Termux task), and to turn its New and Search shortcuts on or off.
The symbols page has Recents on A, as the emoji layer does: the symbols you use most, one press away.
The quick launcher lists your Termux:Widget scripts and tasks (~/.shortcuts) by themselves and keeps them up to date (Apps > Quick Launcher, on by default).
The quick launcher has Flux Keyboard's own shortcuts for the apps in its shortcut and Enter lists: a new message, post or note, an email to write, and the app's search (type the app's name).

Add a shortcut makes the common ones itself: call or message a contact, a website, and Termux tasks (your ~/.shortcuts scripts, run as Termux:Widget runs them), for the apps that only offer theirs to the home screen.
Learn words you use often: a word that isn't in the dictionary goes into it once you've typed it three times (Suggestions & auto-correction).
Remember emails and phone numbers: ones you type yourself are kept in your dictionary and offered as chips in email and phone fields (Suggestions & auto-correction).
Add a shortcut: put shortcuts from your apps, such as a contact's direct dial, a bookmark or a settings page, in the quick launcher's results (Apps › Quick Launcher).

Background picture: put your own picture behind the keyboard (Keyboard theme). With Auto colours on, the keys go see-through and are shaded against it, dark over a bright picture and light over a dark one, with text in whichever of black or white reads better; Key opacity sets how solid they are. The picture is kept in backups.
After an update, Flux Keyboard offers any recommended settings that differ from yours, listing each one from what you have to what's recommended, with Apply all or Keep mine. Looks are never touched.
Ctrl + Shift + D adds the last word you typed to the dictionary, and the suggestions' “add to dictionary” can be switched off (Auto-correction > Dictionary).
Password fields offer the password you just copied as ⎘ •••••••• (never the text itself), from a password manager too.
Edit keyboard layouts in the app: tap a key to change what it types, then save, restore, copy or export the layout.
Tap SYM for one symbol, or the emoji key for one emoji, without opening a screen; SYM's LED shows it held or locked, and a fifth LED does the same for the emoji key.
Trackpad swipes: left, up or right picks that suggestion, and swipe down deletes the previous word (options).
The quick launcher lists apps' own shortcuts, and Back from Niagara's search returns to the app you were in.
One-time codes from your notifications, offered as a chip in the next text field.
The keyboard can take its colours from your wallpaper.
Each app can remember the language you last typed in there.

highlights: GIF search, a dedicated emoji picker key, emoji layer profiles that follow the app, and symbol search.
Spell checking and password-manager autofill in every app.
App shortcuts that work the same in every app.
Made for the Titan 2 Elite: a fitted status bar, per-LED colours, a customisable menu bar and recommended settings.
Settings grouped by task, searchable, and hiding what your phone can't use.
Terminal mode for Termux, and hidden-keyboard apps.
Pick suggestions with Ctrl+Shift+Q, W or E (Right Shift too); Backspace undoes an auto-replace.

improvements.text: Flux Keyboard's New and Search shortcuts reach every app that offers those screens, going by its category, not only the apps in its lists.

The tutorial is reordered: set up, then typing, emoji and symbols, moving around, your apps and the quick launcher, your choices and the look, and last the extras that need a permission, now including running your Termux scripts.
Voice input: choose how long a pause ends it, from 1 to 20 seconds (Modifiers & keys, with Keep listening on).
The symbols page's defaults put your currency on N (from Keyboard > Currency symbol, or the phone's region) and $ on M (€ if yours is $), with ~ on K.
Edit Emoji Layer and Edit Symbols Layer show the search, GIF and Recents keys greyed out, as they aren't mapped.

The emoji and symbol pages have a close key of their own in the bottom-right corner, the same size as the bottom-left one. The switch between emoji and symbols is only there without an emoji key, and the search, GIF and Recents keys stand out in the centred layout too.
Titan 2 Elite LEDs follow the keys left to right (Shift, Alt, Sym, Ctrl, then the emoji key) in rainbow order: green, yellow, blue, purple and pink.
Settings: Titan 2 layout alignment is off by default, and suggestion swipes need a swipe of 150 by default.
Shortcuts for compatible apps can be turned off on their own (Apps > Quick Launcher).
Settings search groups its results under the settings categories, the best-matching category first, so you can see where each setting lives.
Capital after an emoticon: a text emoticon such as :) ;D or <3 ends a sentence like a full stop, so the next word gets a capital (Typing, on by default).
Over a background picture, popups (accents, variations, skin tones) take the picture's colour, lightened or darkened to stay readable, instead of a flat grey.
Long-press an app in the quick launcher to add one of its shortcuts (a contact's direct dial, a bookmark) straight from there.
Clean copied links now works everywhere: a link you copy (YouTube's si and ab_channel included) is cleaned on the clipboard itself, so any app's Paste gets the clean link.
Incognito typing now learns nothing at all: no new words, emails or numbers, word use, or recent emoji, symbols and GIFs. Words are never learned from password, email or web address fields.
Translations updated.
Emoticons keep their shape: punctuation typed straight into more, as in :-) ;( :D, gets no space after it (Typing › Punctuation). Double Space for a full stop is now off by default.
Release notes link to Flux Keyboard's own changelog, and What's new never fetches Pastiera's website notes
Setting links (hold a setting) are Flux Keyboard's own, fluxkeyboard://setting/…: they open the setting in the app and no longer point at Pastiera's website
Straight corner buttons reach down to the bottom edge and out to the side on every page
Straight LEDs are the default and the recommended style on every phone; contoured LEDs stay an option on the Titan 2 Elite
Contoured LEDs rise the same height up the display's sides on every page
Contoured LEDs: the corner buttons on every page (symbol pages, emoji picker, close button) follow the display corners with the same gap inside the LEDs
Contoured LEDs, lit and unlit, draw on every page (symbols, emoji, menu bar) at the same height, and the corner buttons follow a new calibration straight away
Titan 2 Elite display corners default to a shape calibrated on the phone itself: 105 % of the reported curve, slightly squarer, 0.75 px inside the edge
After applying the recommended settings, Make it yours ends with a Done button
Background picture: rotate it a quarter turn at a time
Phone trackpad settings open the Scroll assistant page directly: the mode suggestion swipes and flicks need
Trackpad suggestion swipes: sliding from one key onto the next picks a suggestion, from anywhere on the keys, even slowly
Contoured LEDs: unlit LEDs draw over everything too, filling the corners like lit ones
The intro tutorial covers what's new: Enter per app, background pictures, contoured LEDs, punctuation spacing, hidden-keyboard apps and in-app updates
Background picture: a preview of the bar over your picture, where you drag the picture into place and zoom in; the keyboard frames it the same way. Reset position puts it back.

Note-taking and writing apps (Keep, Obsidian, Notion, OneNote, Docs and others, plus any app Android lists as productivity) keep Enter for a new line, like email apps; Ctrl+Enter does the app's own action, and sends an email.

Restricted settings explained: switching on something Android blocks for apps installed from a file (one-time codes, the accessibility service) shows how to allow it step by step, with a button to App info. The tutorial's Extras page does too.

Recommended settings are now the whole configuration from Flux Keyboard's own Titan 2 Elite, sliders included: auto-correct off, GIFs and one-time codes on, colours from the wallpaper, and the built-in themes' key sizes. Only your languages and app lists are left as they are.
Enter sends in every app by default, with Shift+Enter for a new line (email apps keep Enter for a new line and Ctrl+Enter to send). The new alternative: Enter for a new line, Shift+Enter sends.
Termux:X11 keeps the keyboard hidden by default, like Niagara Launcher.

Recommended settings updated: Ctrl+Space switches layout (not Alt+Shift), no automatic Shift in search fields, punctuation spacing for . , ; : ! ?, and on the Titan 2 Elite contoured LEDs and the lightest trackpad flick.
Enter per app: every chat and email app you have gets its own entry, set to its category (including apps outside the built-in list, by Android's own app category), so each one is there to change.
Punctuation spacing explains itself: each mark is named, with No space before and Space after columns. Space after comma is gone, since the comma's row does it (if it was on, it moves there).
Contoured LEDs on every screen: SYM and emoji pages and the clipboard too.
Terminal apps: no microphone button on the bar or in the menu.

The keyboard follows your phone's dark and light mode with Pastiera's Classic Midnight and Classic Cloud themes, now its only built-in ones; a keyboard still coloured like one of the old ones moves to them. Your own and saved themes stay.

Trackpad & gestures moved into Suggestions & auto-correction, with its sensitivity sliders on the same page. Adding words by gesture greys out while suggestions are off, the sliders show only with a trackpad, they go much lower, and a flick across one key is enough by default on the Titan 2 Elite. Ctrl+Shift+Q/W/E starts off when trackpad swipes pick suggestions.

Settings: "Type to search" on the emoji and symbols layers, "Automatic Shift", a description of what accent & spelling marks do, and the tutorial's Niagara step switches back to the built-in quick launcher too.
The menu bar starts with the everyday buttons: symbols, emoji, GIF, Solderina and keyboard mode are opt-in, and the language button stays hidden while only one language is on.
The quick launcher finds app actions, device controls and navigation actions by default, and in terminal mode the emoji key is Alt until you choose otherwise.
Symbols is the only SYM layer until you turn on others: the emoji and device layers start off, and the search key moves to Q with Recents on A.

Titan 2 Elite: straight corner buttons with filled corners and the 5 dp lift are the default again, contoured LEDs an option, and the LEDs always draw above the bar so the corner buttons never cover them.
Titan 2 Elite: one Corner style choice, Contoured LEDs or Straight buttons (which lift the bar a fixed 5 dp). Fill corners switches itself off with contoured LEDs.
Display contour calibration is in English, lives in Developer options, and sets how far inside the display edge the LED rail runs.

Recommended settings are a short list that suits everyone, with an Apply button that then offers to go through your choices (auto-correct, GIFs, colours) in the tutorial. Nothing personal from the old built-in configuration is applied any more.
Developer options are on by default in dev builds and off in full releases, and the Dev builds switch lives there.
Deleting a word with a trackpad swipe is one choice: off, swipe left or swipe down. Left isn't offered while swipe directions pick suggestions.

Settings tidied: search options for the pickers have a page of their own, one-tap SYM is with the other modifiers, the emoji key LED is with the LED colours, and the quick launcher is called that everywhere.
Trackpad sensitivity has its own slider for left and right suggestion swipes.
The emoji key's LED is pink and SYM's a deeper purple by default.
Shift + Backspace (Settings > Typing > Editing keys) deletes the character after the cursor on the Titan too: it now sees a held Shift.
Updates can offer dev builds too, or only full releases (Settings > Privacy & system > Developer options); dev builds start on dev updates, full releases on releases.
The emoji key has its own status LED by default.
The quick launcher is the built-in one by default, in your keyboard theme's colours.
Automatic Shift stays off in the kinds of field you turn off, and search, links and email start off.
Holding SYM or the emoji key without choosing anything just lets go; trackpad swipes count when short or slanted.
Choose which kinds of text field start with a capital: text, names and addresses by default.
Search bars an app focuses on its own can keep the keyboard bar hidden until you type.
Android's restricted settings are detected, with a way to lift them for one-time codes and the accessibility service.
A shortcut to the phone's own trackpad scroll and cursor settings, in Settings and the quick launcher.
Extras that need a permission or another app start off, and the tutorial sets them up.
What's new closes with ✕ and, after an update, lists only what's new since your version.
Settings search keeps your query and your place when you come back from a result.
Status LED colours in one table, and Input Languages laid out like the other pages.
In Termux, the emoji key can work as Alt.
Search, Recents and GIF keys on the layers have their own tint, with nothing hidden under them; the symbols pencil edits the layer again.
After an update, What's new shows alone, and updates download and install from the app.

improvements: Paste what you just copied from a chip, with tracking stripped from links.
Emoji suggestions, Enter standards by app category, and exact typing in the apps you pick.
Offline mode: nothing in the keyboard goes online.
Updates come from Flux Keyboard's own releases, with the APK one tap away.
Snippets fill in the date, time and clipboard.
Voice input keeps listening through pauses.
Smart Alt and Ctrl, and incognito typing.
Ctrl+Shift+Space switches language backwards; bold suggestions option.
The quick launcher opens from other apps and the app icon.
Pastiera Flux is now Flux Keyboard, at the Pastiera team's request: restore a backup from Pastiera Flux, then uninstall it.

upstream.text: Up to date with Pastiera 0.86, Pastiera's final feature release: its latest changes are merged in, and Flux Keyboard keeps following its security fixes.

Titan 2 Elite: contour LEDs, now Flux Keyboard's default corner style. One LED rail follows the calibrated display curve under the rounded corner buttons, each LED lighting a quarter (or a fifth with the emoji LED).
The menu bar shows SYM while it is held, and the navigation bar under the keyboard takes the keyboard's colour.
About can export a software bill of materials (CycloneDX) for release builds.

upstream: Clicks Power Keyboard support: controls, firmware status and SYM profiles for Razr and Pixel.
An on-screen keyboard mode with themes, a number row, layout styles and long-press layers.
Keyboard themes with an editor, per-app theme assignment and transparent presets.
Titan 2 Elite geometry: rounded corners on the keyboard and status bar, and a gapless mode.
Settings overhauled, with search and shareable deep links.
Learned next-word suggestions, suggestions from several dictionaries, and adding words from a swipe.
Snippet expansion, and emoji and symbol shortcodes.
Configurable punctuation spacing (French spacing, brackets, commas) and smart quotes.
Native trackpad gestures on the Titan 2 and Titan 2 Elite, with separate sensitivities.
Original Titan support, a unified QuickLauncher with Niagara search, and Home and document navigation actions.
Configurable modifier latching and indicators, Alt+Enter layout switching, and bounce keys.
Greek translation, and clipboard history hidden while the phone is locked.
Safer backups (themes and typing sounds included) and many fixes, from Telegram suggestions to Firefox accents.

bugFixes.text: The space after a colon waits for the next key, so :v or :T stays an emoticon and only a word gets the space
Automatic capitals work in apps that keep invisible characters in an empty field or fill it in late, such as Instagram and Keep
Emoji and symbol search no longer gets a capital from the app's automatic capital or Shift
Double-tapping Shift gives Caps Lock at the start of a sentence too, where an automatic capital was already on
Ctrl switches off after an app shortcut such as Ctrl+F, and doesn't carry into the search it opens, so typing there isn't taken for more shortcuts
Shift + Enter makes a new line in WhatsApp again
Words not in a restored backup no longer come back into your dictionary
The Add a shortcut page is laid out like the other settings pages, with readable names and each shortcut's app
Shift, Ctrl and Alt turn on reliably with a slower press, and tapping Shift back on no longer gives Caps Lock
Enter searches in search boxes and one-line fields, such as the Play Store's, instead of making a new line
Spell check no longer marks won't, can't, shan't or elisions such as l'homme as mistakes
An interrupted save can no longer lose your autocorrect words, SYM mappings, input styles or recent symbols
On Android 12 and older, other apps can no longer type into your fields through the keyboard's voice typing
Double space no longer adds a full stop after a comma, colon or bracket
A GIF still downloading when you switch app or field is no longer sent there
The quick launcher opens an app once when Enter is held, and says when something can't be opened
Space after punctuation leaves numbers, times and decimals together (1,000  12:30  3.14)
Checking the Clicks keyboard's firmware version no longer crashes without the Nearby devices permission
The switches on the tutorial's Your choices page show what's really set, even right after applying the recommended settings.
The quick launcher closes smoothly with the Back gesture too, as with the Back key
Background pictures from the camera appear the right way up, instead of sideways
Straight corner buttons on the symbol and emoji pages reach the sides and bottom too, instead of being rounded off
Backups include the Titan 2 Elite display corner calibration
No automatic space after full stops and other punctuation in email, sign-in, web address and password fields
Symbols layer: ~ is on A, instead of hiding under the search key on Q and leaving A empty.

Titan 2 Elite with rounded buttons: the square corners outside the display's curve are filled with the keyboard's colour instead of showing the app behind it (as in screenshots); not with contoured LEDs.
Updates: allowing Flux Keyboard to install apps no longer loses the update. It downloads first, and installs when you come back from Android's switch.
Enter per app's chat standard works in chat apps whose message box asks Android to keep Enter as a new line (Instagram, Snapchat and most others).
The spell checker no longer underlines part of a word with an apostrophe ("couldn't", "it's", "Sam's"), and typing "i'm", "i've", "i'd" or "i'll" corrects to I'm, I've, I'd and I'll.
The clipboard button keeps its place in the menu bar when it shows a count; the count floats in its corner.
A locked Ctrl lets go once an app shortcut has run, so the next key types normally (Nav Mode's Ctrl stays).
Automatic Shift works at the start of a new note in Keep, a new chat message, and WhatsApp's box after sending, where the field wasn't readable yet when it opened.
Passwords copied from a password manager no longer go into the clipboard history.
Phone trackpad settings search for "Keyboard gesture", the page's exact name.
Back cancels a tapped SYM or emoji key that's waiting for its one key, as it closes the symbols.
GIF search no longer keeps every search's results forever: those unused for a week go.
A notification that only mentions "security" (a security briefing, an update) is no longer taken for a one-time code.
The paste chip no longer shows a broken character when the copied text is cut in the middle of an emoji.
After an update with nothing new to tell, What's new no longer opens with every change since Pastiera 0.85.
Updates never miss a release, however many dev builds there are: they read the list of releases in full.
When a message has several numbers, the one next to "code" is offered as the one-time code, not an order or account number.
Delivery and other notifications that only contain "pin" inside a word ("shipping", "Pinterest") are no longer mistaken for one-time codes.
A one-time code you've typed isn't offered again when its message's notification updates.
Updates set to full releases only still find the latest release after many dev builds.
Automatic Shift, auto-correct and replacements work in every text box again with exact typing for no-suggestion fields on.
On the Niagara home screen, SYM + Space opens the quick launcher instead of an empty symbols panel, and Back from Niagara's search returns to your app without pressing Back there too.

bugFixes: No automatic Shift in scripts without capitals, such as Thai.
Letters on the emoji layer and symbols pages type their mappings.
introSince: What's new in Flux Keyboard since the version you had.
